statement: Let n = len(intervals), s = newInterval[0], e = newInterval[1], and let U = {x ∈ ℝ | (s ≤ x ≤ e) or (there exists i with 0 ≤ i < n and intervals[i][0] ≤ x ≤ intervals[i][1])}. The function returns a result r (it does not fail) such that, writing m = len(r) and r[j] = [a_j, b_j] for each 0 ≤ j < m, the following hold: m ≥ 1; every r[j] has length 2 and a_j ≤ b_j; for every 0 ≤ j < m-1, b_j < a_{j+1}; and for every real x, x ∈ U iff there exists j with 0 ≤ j < m and a_j ≤ x ≤ b_j. Thus r is exactly the sorted list of the connected components of U.
preconditions: len(intervals) <= 10000; len(newInterval) = 2; 0 <= newInterval[0] <= newInterval[1] <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(intervals), len(intervals[i]) = 2 and 0 <= intervals[i][0] <= intervals[i][1] <= 100000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(intervals)-1, intervals[i][1] < intervals[i+1][0].

statement: The function returns a result r (i.e., it does not fail, overflow, panic, or go out of bounds) for every input satisfying the preconditions.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the output intervals are strictly ordered and pairwise non-overlapping: for every j with 0 ≤ j < len(r)-1, writing r[j] = [a_j, b_j] and r[j+1] = [a_{j+1}, b_{j+1}], we have b_j < a_{j+1}. Consequently a_j < a_{j+1} for all such j.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, no point of the input intervals or of newInterval is lost: for every real x, if (newInterval[0] ≤ x ≤ newInterval[1]) or (there exists i with 0 ≤ i < len(intervals) and intervals[i][0] ≤ x ≤ intervals[i][1]), then there exists j with 0 ≤ j < len(r) such that r[j][0] ≤ x ≤ r[j][1].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, any input interval that does not intersect newInterval appears unchanged in r. More formally, for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(intervals), if intervals[i][1] < newInterval[0] or newInterval[1] < intervals[i][0], then there exists j with 0 ≤ j < len(r) such that r[j][0] = intervals[i][0] and r[j][1] = intervals[i][1].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the whole newInterval is contained in exactly one output interval. That is, there exists j with 0 ≤ j < len(r) such that r[j][0] ≤ newInterval[0] and newInterval[1] ≤ r[j][1]; and for every k with 0 ≤ k < len(r) and k ≠ j, the interval r[k] does not intersect [newInterval[0], newInterval[1]] (i.e., r[k][1] < newInterval[0] or newInterval[1] < r[k][0]).
